language.script_notes: Catalan appears bilingually (and often primarily) on signage in Catalonia/Valencia/the Balearics — visually distinct with doubled 'l·l' and accented vowels.
false_friends: Morocco/North Africa (Moorish architectural influence in Andalusia)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Orange reflectors common on coastal highway guardrails.
road_furniture.curb_style: Dense modernist street furniture in Barcelona specifically (distinctive tiled sidewalks, ornate lampposts).

architecture.roof_style: Flat or very low-pitch roofs common in the arid Andalusian interior; standard terracotta pitched roofs along the Mediterranean coast and in Catalonia.
architecture.roof_material: Flat roofs increase toward the drier south.
architecture.wall_construction: Whitewashed masonry is the defining Andalusian look ('pueblos blancos'), often with Moorish/Mudéjar architectural details (horseshoe arches, tilework, courtyards) reflecting centuries of Islamic rule; Gaudí/Catalan modernist architecture and dense stucco apartment blocks in Barcelona.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Brilliant whitewash is the single strongest Andalusian tell; warm Mediterranean stucco tones along the Costa del Sol/Costa Brava; Barcelona's colourful modernist facades.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Whitewashed pueblos blancos built into cliff faces (Setenil de las Bodegas); Moorish palace architecture (Alhambra-style arches and tilework); Gaudí's modernist Barcelona landmarks; dense Mediterranean resort development along the coast.

nature.vegetation: Dense grid-planted olive groves cover huge stretches of the Andalusian interior; Mediterranean scrub, palm trees and citrus orchards along the coast; noticeably more cactus/succulent and arid vegetation in the southeast (Almería).
nature.terrain: The Sierra Nevada and Sierra de Grazalema mountains rise behind a warm Mediterranean/Atlantic coastline; the Guadalquivir river valley cuts through Andalusia; the Catalan/Valencian coast is a long, developed Mediterranean shoreline.
nature.climate_signature: Classic hot, dry, sun-bleached Mediterranean light — brighter and more intense than central or northern Spain, with silvery olive-grove hillsides a recurring visual signature.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Heavy tourist/rental car presence along the Costa del Sol.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 4 around Barcelona, Seville, Valencia and Málaga.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very dense along the coast and in major cities; thinner in the remote Andalusian sierra interior.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Dry farmland, similar hot summer climate
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Andalusia has whitewashed pueblos blancos, dense olive-grove grids and Moorish architectural detail; the Meseta is a flatter, higher wheat-farming plateau without the whitewash or Moorish arches.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Whitewashed Mediterranean hill towns, similar bright coastal light, olive groves
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Spain's bollard is wedge-shaped with orange/white reflectors vs. Italy's red-diagonal post; Spanish vocabulary ('Calle') and Moorish arch details differ from Italian 'Via' signage and Italy's terracotta-dominant roofing.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Moorish/Andalusian architectural heritage — horseshoe arches, tilework, courtyard houses
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Spain uses Latin script and Spanish/Catalan language with EU blue-strip plates; Morocco uses Arabic script (plus French) and different plate styles, and drives on the right but with visibly different road infrastructure and vehicle stock.
